<thought>Based on the mass spectrum, the molecular ion is at m/z 127.0997, which matches the monoisotopic mass of the formula C₇H₁₃NO (C 7 × 12.0000 = 84.0000; H 13 × 1.007825 = 13.1017; N = 14.0031; O = 15.9949; total = 127.0997). The M+1 intensity (~8 %) is consistent with ~7‑8 carbons (13C natural abundance ≈ 1.1 % per carbon). The formula gives a double‑bond equivalent (DBE) of 2, indicating either a carbonyl plus one additional double bond/ring, typical for an amide. A plausible structure fitting C₇H₁₃NO is **N‑methyl‑butanamide** (CH₃CH₂CH₂C(=O)NHCH₃), whose SMILES is `CCCC(=O)NC`. This structure satisfies the formula, DBE, and common functional groups expected for the observed spectra.**
